outcome: Heterogeneity syntax completed: named dimensions, rest_of_group, nesting, read-only traits
owner_impact: The syntax you shaped today is live. Every group names its dimension; rest_of_group replaces rest=True; within= nests a split inside a group, so a paper's exact joint counts (e.g. 10 malicious among 40 informed) are expressible, while separate dimensions stay independent. Values given to groups are traits: the Controller declares them as informed = trait(False) and can only read them; Initialization gives them with set_trait("informed", "informed", True). True/False is supported. The full guide is docs/HETEROGENEITY_GUIDE.md. Your three Experiments are migrated with the same robots and values, and republished to the Showcase. Test now: yes. Open Constant Bearing Flocking from the Showcase; the setup message should read 'Groups: information: informed 80, uninformed 120'.

next.text: #577 release 5: statements (local names, if/elif/else) in the environment field function, the last part of the one-grammar work. It has not started yet.

technical_evidence: Initializer: splits keyed by (dimension, within), dealt in declaration order from initialization stream 1 + order (the first split reproduces the previous deal); overlap-based conflict checks for traits and sensors; retired forms raise errors naming the replacement.

Controller: NAME = trait(default) with number or True/False, read-only (compile error on assignment, also rejected by the Rust runtime); Rust stores bool traits as 1/0 and loads them as booleans; cross-validation requires set_trait targets to be declared traits of the same type.

Equivalence: of 28,989 cases, all changes are explained (Initialization sources using heterogeneity syntax, Controller sources using trait, and one reworded class-attribute error). Reference trajectories unchanged; all 5 reference runs bit-identical on the rebuilt WebAssembly kernel.
